slides.text: top 5 back exercises, ranked by how easy they are to progress on

slides.image_direction: REAL FOUNDER PHOTO: crop and resize only, face and physique unchanged
slides.text:
ranked for beginner to intermediate lifters:
small jumps, a setup you can repeat, safe to push alone.

slides.image_direction: REAL FOUNDER PHOTO: crop and resize only, face and physique unchanged
slides.text:
#5 pull-ups
brilliant, but hard to progress in small steps until you can do plenty of reps.

slides.image_direction: REAL FOUNDER PHOTO: crop and resize only, face and physique unchanged
slides.text:
#4 barbell row
form drifts as you tire, so last week's numbers are hard to compare.

slides.image_direction: REAL FOUNDER PHOTO: crop and resize only, face and physique unchanged
slides.text:
#3 single-arm dumbbell row
quick to set up. dumbbell jumps are big, so add reps first.

slides.image_direction: REAL FOUNDER PHOTO: crop and resize only, face and physique unchanged
slides.text:
#2 chest-supported row
the pad stops the swing, so each session compares cleanly to the last.

bonus tip: if you can't compare sessions, you can't progress.
i'm building EARND for that.

slides.image_direction: REAL FOUNDER PHOTO: crop and resize only, face and physique unchanged
slides.text:
#1 lat pulldown
pin stack, small jumps, the same setup every time. the easiest to beat.
